bug_description.normalized: The exact staged reproducing checkout is ancestor `fd85818b5b85fb0ad2db71c60e94ca0689d38bca`, not metadata vulnerable commit `5532374f61284a254d5b2a8de9472c64f138c854`, but the vulnerable `sbix` code and `hb-subset-fuzzer.cc` call sites are unchanged between them. Stage 01 reproduced the crash with `hb-subset-fuzzer` reading the 98811-byte saved `poc`; ASan frame 10 is `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` at `test/fuzzing/hb-subset-fuzzer.cc:85`, so the first fixed-text `trySubset()` call reached `hb_subset()` and `_subset_table`'s `HB_OT_TAG_sbix` case. In `OT::sbix::add_strike()`, HarfBuzz materializes one serialized strike offset into a concrete `SBIXStrike` and `available_len`. Inside `OT::SBIXStrike::subset()`, the vulnerable guard for one mapped `old_gid` checks only offset order, minimum size, and the upper bound. On the crashing path `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid]` is null while `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1]` is a larger in-range offset, so the guard passes and `delta` plus `glyph_data_length` are derived from that null-start pair. `this + imageOffsetsZ[old_gid]` therefore resolves to `Null(SBIXGlyph)` backed by global `_hb_NullPool`, yet `SBIXGlyph::copy()` still forwards the positive `glyph_data_length` to `data.copy()`. `hb_array_t::copy()` then reads past `_hb_NullPool`, and AddressSanitizer reports `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/hb-array.hh:220`. The fix commit expresses the missing obligation by adding `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid].is_null()` and `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1].is_null()` to the `SBIXStrike::subset()` guard, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

The patch fixes this exact obligation by adding `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid].is_null()` and `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1].is_null()` here.

first_subset_call.description: ASan frame 10 points to the first fixed-text `trySubset()` call at line 85, not the later data-derived call at line 98. The observed crash path therefore uses the built-in ASCII test glyph set and `flags[0] == 0`.

evidence_limitations: The saved artifacts do not reveal which exact strike index or `new_gid`/`old_gid` pair satisfied the vulnerable guard; the fine trace therefore stays at the first selected pair required by `SBIXStrike::subset()` rather than naming a speculative glyph.
Runtime disambiguation was disabled in `run_flags.json`, so Stage 02 used only the saved reproduction and source artifacts; it did not execute the fixed image or add marker instrumentation.

coarse_trace.summary: During the first fixed-text subset call, HarfBuzz reaches the `sbix` table and materializes one serialized strike offset into a concrete `SBIXStrike` plus the remaining-byte bound `available_len`.
The strike subsetter selects a mapped glyph and accepts a null start offset because the guard checks only offset order, minimum size, and the upper bound, not `is_null()`.

The unchecked offset pair is turned into `glyph_data_length`, and the null offset is dereferenced as `Null(SBIXGlyph)` from `_hb_NullPool` while the positive length is forwarded to the glyph-data copy.
Byte-copy code reads `glyph_data_length` bytes from the null glyph's `data` field and eventually reads past global `_hb_NullPool`, matching the saved ASan global-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. In the `sbix` subsetting path, `add_strike()` first evaluates the attacker-controlled strike offset `strikes[i]`. On the crashing path it is non-null and within `sbix_len`, so the call materializes the selected `SBIXStrike` and the bound `available_len = sbix_len - strikes[i]` used by later glyph-offset checks. ASan frame 4 shows this executed during the first fixed-text `trySubset()` call at `hb-subset-fuzzer.cc:85`.

fine_trace.code:
if (!c->plan->old_gid_for_new_gid (new_gid, &old_gid) ||
    unlikely (imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1] <= imageOffsetsZ[old_gid] ||
              imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1] - imageOffsetsZ[old_gid] <= SBIXGlyph::min_size) ||
              (unsigned int) imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1] > available_len)
fine_trace.note: Root cause. For one mapped `old_gid` selected by the subset plan, this guard reads the start and end glyph offsets from the strike but only checks ordering, minimum size, and the upper bound. On the crashing path `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid]` is the null offset while `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1]` is a larger in-range offset, so the guard does not continue even though the start offset is null. The patch fixes this exact obligation by adding `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid].is_null()` and `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1].is_null()` here.

fine_trace.code:
unsigned int delta = imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1] - imageOffsetsZ[old_gid];
unsigned int glyph_data_length = delta - SBIXGlyph::min_size;
fine_trace.note: The unchecked offset pair from step 2 is converted into the byte count later copied. Because the start offset is null on the crashing path, `delta` equals the successor offset and `glyph_data_length` becomes that offset minus the fixed 8-byte `SBIXGlyph` header.

depends_on.via: !c->plan->old_gid_for_new_gid (new_gid, &old_gid) || unlikely (imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1] <= imageOffsetsZ[old_gid] || imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1] - imageOffsetsZ[old_gid] <= SBIXGlyph::min_size) || (unsigned int) imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1] > available_len)

fine_trace.note: The start offset from step 2 is then dereferenced as an `LOffsetTo<SBIXGlyph>`. Because it is null, `OffsetTo::operator()` returns `Null(SBIXGlyph)` backed by global `_hb_NullPool` instead of a glyph inside the font, yet the call still passes the positive `glyph_data_length` from step 3 to `SBIXGlyph::copy()`.

depends_on.via: !c->plan->old_gid_for_new_gid (new_gid, &old_gid) || unlikely (imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1] <= imageOffsetsZ[old_gid] || imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1] - imageOffsetsZ[old_gid] <= SBIXGlyph::min_size) || (unsigned int) imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1] > available_len)

fine_trace.note: `SBIXGlyph::copy()` forwards the attacker-derived `glyph_data_length` as `data_length` to the unsized byte array member of the null glyph object. This treats the null object's `data` field inside `_hb_NullPool` as if it were a real bitmap payload of that length.

fine_trace.code: out[i] = arrayZ[i]; /* TODO: add version that calls c->copy() */
fine_trace.note: Sink. `UnsizedArrayOf::copy()` turns the null glyph's `data` member into `count = data_length` bytes and this loop reads each `arrayZ[i]`. Because `arrayZ` points into `_hb_NullPool` while `count` comes from the unchecked offset delta, the loop eventually reads 1 byte past `_hb_NullPool`, matching the saved ASan `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `hb-array.hh:220` and the report that the address is 0 bytes to the right of global `_hb_NullPool` defined in `src/hb-static.cc:42`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports that the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of global `_hb_NullPool` defined here with size 384.

Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The missing null-offset guard in `SBIXStrike::subset()` turns `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid] == 0` into `Null(SBIXGlyph)`, which is backed by the exact global object `_hb_NullPool` that ASan reports as overflowed.

format.name: OpenType/sfnt font with sbix table
format.contract: The saved artifacts establish only the exact staged witness font. When `hb-subset-fuzzer` processes this `poc`, the first fixed-text `trySubset()` call (`LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` frame at `test/fuzzing/hb-subset-fuzzer.cc:85`) reaches `OT::sbix::subset()`. For at least one selected strike and mapped glyph, `SBIXStrike::subset()` sees `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid] == 0` and a larger in-range `imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1]`; because the vulnerable guard omits `is_null()` checks, `SBIXGlyph::copy()` treats `Null(SBIXGlyph)` from `_hb_NullPool` as real glyph data and `hb_array_t::copy()` performs the observed `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 1`. The saved artifacts do not reveal the exact strike index or `old_gid`, so this contract should not be generalized beyond this witness.
